caption:
Brampton new build. Second tax bill?

When you buy a newly built home, a supplementary tax bill may follow after you move in. 1) Early tax bills on a new build may reflect only the vacant land. 2) After you move in, MPAC values the finished home and sends a Property Assessment Change Notice. 3) The City of Brampton says a new house is often assessed from the occupancy or closing date; the City of Mississauga says the bill can cover the current and up to two previous years, prorated from the effective date. 4) It is a separate bill that does not replace your regular bills, so budget for it. If your mortgage payment includes taxes, the bill may go to your lender. Instalments and due dates vary by municipality: check your own bill and the Property Assessment Change Notice.
Sources: City of Brampton, "Supplementary Tax Bill" (brampton.ca); Town of Milton, "Assessments" (milton.ca); City of Mississauga, "Supplementary tax bill" (mississauga.ca, page dated Jul 14, 2025), all checked Nov 24, 2026.

Sell within a year? Fully taxable.

The Canada Revenue Agency's residential property flipping rule has applied since January 1, 2023. 1) A home owned for less than 365 consecutive days before it is sold is generally treated as a flipped property. 2) The profit is fully taxable as business income and does not qualify for the principal residence exemption or the 50 per cent capital gains inclusion rate. 3) Exceptions can apply for certain life events, such as a death, a household change like a new child, a separation, a safety threat, serious illness or disability, an involuntary job loss, a work or study relocation, insolvency or the loss of the property. 4) Your own situation decides, so talk to a tax professional before you list.
Source: Canada Revenue Agency, "Residential property flipping rule" (canada.ca, page modified Oct 21, 2024), checked Nov 24, 2026.

$700K, low down payment. Hidden cost?

Example only, for a $700,000 home with the minimum down payment:
1) Minimum down payment: 5% of the first $500,000 + 10% of the other $200,000 = $45,000.
2) Mortgage needed: $700,000 - $45,000 = $655,000.
3) That is 93.6% of the price. CMHC's premium for 90.01% to 95% loan-to-value is 4.00%: $655,000 x 4.00% = $26,200, which may be added to the mortgage.
4) Mortgage you carry: $655,000 + $26,200 = $681,200.
Ontario sales tax (8% of the premium, about $2,096) cannot be added to the mortgage and is paid at closing. Sagen and Canada Guaranty also insure mortgages, and each sets its own premiums. Closing costs are extra, and lenders and insurers set the final terms, so confirm your numbers with your lender.

caption:
New build. $50,000 rebate. Eligible?

The Canada Revenue Agency's first-time home buyers' GST/HST rebate covers newly built or substantially renovated homes. 1) You must be 18 or older, a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, and a first-time buyer under the CRA's test (not having lived in a home you or your spouse owned in the current or previous four calendar years). The home must be your primary residence. 2) The agreement of purchase and sale must be signed on or after March 20, 2025 (and before 2031). At or below $1 million the rebate is up to 100% of the GST (or federal part of the HST), to a maximum of $50,000. 3) Between $1 million and $1.5 million the maximum is gradually reduced; at $1.5 million or more there is no rebate. 4) With a builder purchase, the builder usually files, and the forms (GST190 and RC7190-ON) are signed with the builder or your lawyer around closing. Ontario has a separate first-time buyer rebate on the provincial part of the HST: see the CRA page for details. Eligibility rules apply.
Source: Canada Revenue Agency, "First-time home buyers' (FTHB) GST/HST rebate" (canada.ca, pages modified Mar to Oct 2026), checked Nov 24, 2026.

caption:
Kitchener condo signed. Missed 10 days?

Myth: once you sign for a new condo, you are locked in. Fact: under section 73(2) of Ontario's Condominium Act, buyers of a new condo have a 10-day cooling-off period in which they may rescind their agreement of purchase and sale. Tarion says the period begins on the later of the date you receive the agreement of purchase and sale, the disclosure documents and the Condo Guide. Use that window to review everything with your lawyer, because after it ends you may no longer be able to rescind. This applies to new condo purchases from a developer, not resale condos.
Source: Tarion, "Building and selling condominiums" (tarion.com), checked Nov 24, 2026.

Old attic insulation. Asbestos risk?

Quick tip: Health Canada says some vermiculite insulation may contain asbestos. If a home you are buying has it in the attic or walls, the guidance is to leave it undisturbed, not use the attic for storage, not try to remove it yourself, and hire professionals trained to handle asbestos before any renovation. Ask your home inspector to flag attic insulation, and talk to your Realtor® about what to ask the seller.
Source: Health Canada, "Asbestos and your health" (canada.ca, page modified Feb 10, 2023), and Employment and Social Development Canada, "Vermiculite Insulation Containing Tremolite Asbestos" (canada.ca), checked Nov 24, 2026.
